title: Oven-Baked Samosa Rolls
subtitle: with Mint Yoghurt Dipping Sauce
description: Turn your favourite Indian snack into dinnertime deliciousness with our clever take on samosas. Fill tortillas with a curried potato and pea filling, then bake until warm and crisp.

steps.text: Boil potato and peas: Peel the potatoes and cut into 2cm chunks. Put in a medium saucepan, cover with cold salted water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 10-12 mins until almost tender. Add the peas and cook for 2 mins or until tender. Drain. Wipe the pan clean with paper towel and reserve.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 220C. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Crush or finely chop 2 garlic cloves. Finely chop the coriander leaves and stems, keeping them separate. Reserve half the mint leaves, then finely chop the remaining leaves, discarding the stems.

Make potato filling: Heat 1 tbs vegetable oil in the reserved pan over medium heat. Cook the garlic, coriander stems and curry powder, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Add the potato and peas, coriander leaves and 20g butter and cook, coarsely mashing with a spoon, for 1-2 mins until well combined. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper.

Assemble and bake: Top each tortilla with 80ml (⅓ cup) potato filling and shape into a log. Roll up each tortilla to enclose the filling. Put the samosa rolls on the lined tray, seam side down, leaving a 1cm gap between each. Generously spray or brush the tops and sides with vegetable oil. Bake for 15-20 mins until golden and crisp.

Serve up: Combine the yoghurt and chopped mint in a bowl. Using a serrated knife, cut the samosa rolls in half on an angle. Scatter over the reserved mint leaves and serve with the mint yoghurt for dipping. Enjoy!
Make it yours: Indian samosas are traditionally served with chutney for dipping. If you have some in your fridge, serve on the side for an authentic (and delicious!) touch.
